plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration.
Add to SPY to increase broad index exposure.
Hold a significant cash buffer for safety.
Focus on capital preservation with tight stops.
conservative.read: This plan prioritizes capital preservation. Expect lower potential returns, around 1.5% per month, with significantly reduced drawdown risk. It aims for stability over aggressive growth.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to minimal levels.
Reduce concentration in METU and MUU.
Buy LMT as a new, high-scoring position.
Increase exposure to the broad QQQ index.
Maintain a moderate cash buffer for flexibility.
balanced.read: This balanced approach seeks risk-first growth, targeting around 2.5% per month. It blends broad market exposure with quality tech and limited leverage. Drawdowns are managed by trimming riskier assets.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and concentrated names (METU, MUU).
Add new high-scoring opportunities like LMT and ADI.
Maintain a smaller cash buffer to maximize invested capital.
Utilize wider stops to allow for volatility.
Concentrate capital in the highest conviction plays.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan aims for stretched growth, targeting around 4% per month. It leans heavily into leverage and concentration, accepting significantly higher potential drawdowns. Daily rebalancing of leveraged ETFs can impact performance.

plan: Sell all leveraged and high-beta single names to zero.
Increase QQQI allocation to 30% for income generation.
Add to SPY for broad market exposure and stability.
Maintain a cash buffer for yield focus.
Prioritize steady monthly distributions over growth.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% per month through distributions. It prioritizes capital preservation and reliable income over growth potential. NAV can still decline in market selloffs, but the focus is on yield.
